newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to boost autonomy for native islanders.
newsitem.headline: Australia to boost autonomy for native islanders.

text.p: Australia, riven by divisive rows over race and indigenous land rights, on Wednesday said it would give native islanders more independence.

Prime Minister John Howard said Torres Strait Islanders living on remote islands between Australia's far north and neighbouring Papua New Guinea would administer their own affairs in a divorce from the peak native body, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission (ATSIC).
Howard, who has been accused of selling out Aborigines and Torres Strait Islanders over land rights, made the announcement on a visit to Thursday Island, off the northern tip of Queensland state.

"It's just that they want to be dealt with differently and separately from the Aboriginal community. It's not that they have any hostility to them, it's just that they are a distinctive group and they clearly are," Howard told reporters,
In origin, the few thousand Islanders are ethnically Melanesian, like their Papua New Guinea neighbours, not Aboriginal.
He said his conservative Liberal-National government would introduce legislation into parliament this year to allow Torres Strait Islanders to administer their own affairs by 2000.
He did not give detail on how the scheme would work.
Local Torres Strait elders welcomed Howard's announcement, but urged formal recognition of the Torres Strait people's prior ownership of the area's land and seas.

"Any separate legislation for Torres Strait must include in the preamble as a general, formal recognition of government to the Torres Strait people, a recognition of Torres Strait Islanders being the prior occupier and original owners of our reefs, our islands and our seas," Thursday Island Coordinating Committee chairman Getano Lui Jr said in a speech.
Native groups have accused Howard of attempting to reduce their land rights in his controversial solution to a divisive row between indigenous Australians and farmers.

He has also been widely criticised for failing to act swiftly and firmly enough against race row politician Pauline Hanson, whose anti-immigration and anti-Aboriginal welfare policies have split the Australian community.
